name: Do I need an engineer to remove an interior wall?

mainEntity.name: Do I need an engineer to remove an interior wall?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Not necessarily. A structural review may find that a beam or support is required even when no load-bearing wall is visible, while a clearly nonstructural partition may not need structural design. The answer depends on the opening, surrounding framing, and local requirements.

Context: Structural engineering, architectural design, permit plans, and construction are separate considerations. Community discussions show that engineering and permits are often priced separately from demolition and finish work.

Key factors:
- Span and loads above
- Existing plans and field measurements
- Beam and post configuration
- Jurisdictional submittal requirements

Practical guidance: Ask whether the proposal includes a structural assessment, stamped or reviewed plans if needed, permit coordination, and inspection support. Elite Remodeling & Design can determine whether the wall removal belongs within a larger design-build scope requiring coordinated plans.

Do not pay for unnecessary design, but do not skip it when the load path is uncertain.
acceptedAnswer.description: Maybe. A verified nonstructural partition may not need structural engineering, but a load-bearing wall or uncertain load path may require structural design, plans, or calculations. Confirm what the jurisdiction and project conditions require.
